analysis:
The PR's only change in both files is a module-qualification of the drafter loader call: `Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load` becomes `MLXLLM.Gemma4AssistantDraftModel.load`, at BackendParityHarness.swift line 435 and MTPProductionSession.swift line 115. Both call sites are in the ProviderBenchmark target, which is a benchmark/parity harness rather than the serving path. The change only resolves a name ambiguity at compile time, probably because MLXVLM now exports a similarly named type. It adds no new inputs, I/O, network surface, key handling, attestation, or authorization logic. The loaded directory is still operator-supplied via `--assistant-model`, as before.

I also read the surrounding harness source. It calls EngineV2Factory.makeProductionBuild with `constructionPurpose: .benchmark`, uses `PrefixCacheV2` (an in-memory cache with fixed scope IDs "g2-parity"), and passes `checkpointQuantization: .native`. Its only logging is to stderr, covering parity prompt names, token counts and finish reasons, using hard-coded prompts, not consumer data. It does not touch the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the KEK, coordinator traffic, or provider keys. No threat-model assumption is invalidated.

One unverified point: whether `MLXLLM.Gemma4AssistantDraftModel` is the same type the previously unqualified call resolved to. Gemma4CBv2MTPDrafter's initializer would fail to compile if the types differed, so this is a build-correctness question, not a security one. I found no security regression.
